17.t: Working with data: a bike dynamo
q: Describe the relationship up to 20 km/h.
Voltage is about proportional to speed: it rises about 1.25 V for every 5 km/h.
Explain why spinning faster gives a bigger voltage.
The magnet turns faster, so the magnetic field through the coil changes faster, inducing a bigger voltage.
The lamp is rated 6 V. Suggest a problem when stopping at traffic lights, and one solution.
At 0 km/h there is no voltage: the light goes out. Use a rechargeable battery or capacitor charged while riding (a "standlight").
